text:
maria: heads up — seeing intermittent packet loss between GPU pods on the same node after yesterday's scale surge. spikes ~0.2-0.6% for short bursts, coincides with pod migrations. :thinking:

tom: any particular kernel logs or dmesg entries?

maria: not much in dmesg, but tcpdump on vxlan0 shows duplicate outer UDP acks + some retransmits. short capture attached (snip):
```
12:34:10.123456 IP nodeA.vxlan > nodeA.vxlan: UDP, length 1420
12:34:10.123789 IP nodeA.vxlan > nodeA.vxlan: UDP, length 64
--- retransmit patterns every ~30s ---
```

junaid: interesting — pods moved between NICs when we did the reprovisioning. could be path migration in the underlay causing out-of-order for fragments?

eli: do we have GSO/GRO/NAPI offload toggles on these NICs? last time similar symptoms we saw offload + vxlan + mtu combos trigger microbursts.

maria: ethtool -k shows gro:on gso:on tso:on on mlx5. tried disabling gro/gso on a test node:
```bash
ethtool -K ens5 gro off gso off tso off
```
loss dropped to near 0 in the minute after but came back when pods moved again.

srebot: note: this thread linked to 2227000001 (autoscaler-reprovision-job) and 2225000002 (gpu-node-autoscale-metrics).

tom: does it reproduce with smaller MTU (e.g. 1400) or by forcing no encapsulation? can you run iperf between containers pinned to same NIC?

maria: ran iperf3 pinned same socket namespace: stable. When VXLAN is in play and pod moves across underlying physical port, we see short loss windows. traceroute shows ECMP hash change:
```
traceroute to nodeA (10.1.2.3), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.0.0.1  0.23 ms  0.17 ms  0.16 ms
 2  10.0.0.9  1.21 ms  1.12 ms  12.11 ms  <-- asymmetric path sometimes
```

junaid: sounds like underlay path migration + offload interaction. could be hardware steering retaining stale flow state so encapsulated fragments get reordered.

eli: can we try two quick experiments: 1) disable LRO/GRO/GSO on NICs for a node pool and run a controlled backfill, 2) pin overlay to single physical port via nodeAffinity to avoid ECMP changes during migration?

maria: already did (1) on a canary node — immediate improvement but not long-term acceptable perf. (2) might help for a short window; I can try scheduling a small rotation to validate.

tom: also check RDMA offload state — if mlx5 RDMA is enabled, flows might be bypassing kernel datapath in odd ways. `ibv_devinfo` + `mlxconfig -d` output would help.

maria: fetched ibv_devinfo, RDMA enabled on the pool. disabling RDMA for canary nodes reduced the spikes in our test.

junaid: ok promising. levers then: 1) prefer node pools with stable port mapping for sensitive jobs, 2) disable offloads or tune HW steering for VXLAN, 3) raise MTU conservatively or use smaller VXLAN payload to avoid fragmentation.

eli: also add a small eBPF filter to mark and trace encapsulated flows during migration windows, so we can correlate with autoscaler events.

maria: will run a canary plan: disable RDMA on 2 nodes, toggle offloads, and run backfill replica job for 30m. I'll post results.

tom: thanks — if you see the pattern keep the captures. we may need vendor escalations with Mellanox if HW steering is dropping frag orders.

maria: noted. adding timeline: canary start 2228463800, end 2228465600. will update thread. :white_check_mark:
